It applies to the full registered chronic-disease population and should be read together with the Cardiovascular Risk and Hypertension guidelines (NHA-CG-02, NHA-CG-03). §2 Glycaemic targets  A target HbA1c below 7.0% is recommended for most adults with Type 2 diabetes.  A relaxed target of up to 8.0% may be appropriate for elderly patients, those with limited life expectancy, advanced complications, or high hypoglycaemia risk.  HbA1c between 7.0% and 8.9% is classified as moderately controlled; 9.0% or above is classified as uncontrolled and requires treatment intensification review within 4 weeks. §3 First-line therapy  Metformin is first-line therapy for Type 2 diabetes unless contraindicated.  Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73m² and the dose should be reviewed and reduced when eGFR is below 45.  Lifestyle intervention (nutrition, physical activi

traindicated.  Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73m² and the dose should be reviewed and reduced when eGFR is below 45.  Lifestyle intervention (nutrition, physical activity, weight management) is indicated at every stage of therapy. §4 Treatment intensification  If HbA1c remains at or above 8.0% on metformin monotherapy after 3 months, add a second agent selected by comorbidity.  A GLP-1 receptor agonist is preferred for patients with BMI above 30 kg/m² or where weight reduction is a priority; it is also appropriate when HbA1c is 8.0% or above despite dual therapy.  An SGLT2 inhibitor is preferred for patients with heart failure or chronic kidney disease stages 3a-3b, subject to eGFR of at least 20-25 depending on agent.  Insulin should be considered when HbA1c is 8.5% or above despite two or more non-insulin agents, or at any point with symptomatic hyperglycaemia. §5 Screening and monitoring intervals  HbA1c: at least every 6 months when stable; every 3 months after any therapy change.  Retinal examination: every 12 months for all patients with diabetes.  Foot examination: every 12 months; high-risk feet every 3-6 months.

A patient whose interval is exceeded is recorded as having an open care gap and enters the recall workflow defined in the Population Screening and Recall Policy (NHA-PP-01 §4). §6 Renal considerations  Review all medication during acute kidney injury; withhold metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors while eGFR is acutely below 30.  Refer to nephrology at CKD stage 4 (eGFR below 30) or with rapidly declining function. §7 Human oversight of AI-assisted recommendations Any medication recommendation produced with the assistance of an analytical model or AI agent is advisory only. A licensed clinician must review and approve the recommendation before any prescription is issued. AI-generated drafts must be recorded with their evidence citations in the audit log.
